---
title: "LCS"
description: |
  The longest common subsequnce problem 
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE)
```

Year ago I was interested in this problem as a potential topic for my PhD thesis. I had some ideas but they did not work out. Here is what I wrote back [then](https://github.com/prabinov42/MiscData/blob/master/LCS.pdf).

I have recently explicitly calculated (not sampled) the distribution of the lengths for the LCS for $n$ up to $16$. The results are [here](https://github.com/prabinov42/LCS_Numerology/blob/main/LCS_Numerology.md). Note that these are done in arbitrary precision math with Mathematica, not floating point approximations. To the best of my knowledge, these have not been published before - certainly not at n=16.
